messages:
maria.gonzalez: Hey team — quick heads up / question. I filed my STEM OPT extension (I-765) on 2026-02-12 and got the receipt notice, but my EAD is still pending. My Redwood offer lists a 2026-04-01 start. I need to travel to Spain 2026-03-20 to 2026-03-30 for a family thing. Two Qs: 1) Is re-entry while I have a pending I-765 a hard no? 2) If payroll starts before my EAD arrives, how do stipend/tax withholdings and benefits enrollment work? Need to coordinate docs for onboarding.

jess.peopleops: Thanks for the heads up, Maria — congrats on the offer 🎉. Short answers: 1) travel while a STEM extension is pending can be risky — depends on consulate/travel docs; we usually advise staying in US until EAD arrives for new hires. 2) Payroll can set up a hire date but we can hold payments until work authorization is in place — let me loop payroll/legal.

raj.legal: Hi Maria — quick legal note: If you're on OPT and have a pending I-765 for STEM, re-entry to the US often requires a valid EAD or an unexpired F-1 with a valid travel signature and I-20 plus proof of pending application; re-admission is at CBP discretion. If you're leaving while receipt is pending and you don't have an unexpired EAD, there's a non-zero risk of being denied boarding/re-entry. Recommend consulting your DSO first. If possible, avoid travel until EAD arrives.

alec.payroll: From payroll side: we can provision payroll records with your offer start, but we cannot release wages without documentation of work authorization. For stipend/expense reimbursements we can hold them or issue them after proof of authorization. Taxes: withholding setup will be in ADP based on forms you submit; no tax consequence to delaying payment aside from timing. If you want, I can schedule a short call to walk through ADP forms.

carla-onboarding: For benefits enrollment: new hires with a confirmed active hire date get a benefits enrollment window (30 days). Benefits eligibility typically requires employment to have started; if the hire date is delayed because of authorization, enrollment window shifts. If we set the hire date but hold pay pending EAD, we might still open enrollment, but benefits cannot be active until cleared with proof of authorization in some carriers. I'll confirm carrier rules.

maria.gonzalez: Thanks — super helpful. My DSO said travel signature on I-20 is valid for 6 months and they signed last week, but I don't have an EAD yet. If the DSO sign-off is technically OK, would Redwood accept that for onboarding docs temporarily? I can upload a scanned I-20 + USCIS receipt.

jess.peopleops: You can upload the receipt + signed I-20 to our onboarding portal now so we have the records — but note legal/payroll still need final EAD before payroll runs. Please add a short note in the upload: "pending EAD - travel dates 2026-03-20 to 2026-03-30" so we can flag the case.

raj.legal: Adding: receipt + signed I-20 helps for documentation but doesn't guarantee CBP readmission. From company compliance POV, we need to verify you are authorized to work before paying wages. If you return with an unexpired I-20 and DSO travel endorsement, it's often fine for re-entry; still a small risk.

alec.payroll: Maria — if you want to avoid payment delays, options: (A) delay start until after EAD arrives, (B) keep start date but agree in writing that payroll will be suspended until you provide EAD; we can do (B) but will need a signed acknowledgement form. Which would you prefer?

maria.gonzalez: I prefer not to delay start if possible. I'll upload receipt + I-20 now and sign the payroll acknowledgement if needed. One more: will unpaid stipend reimbursements (travel/relocation) be taxable if issued after start vs before? I was told relocation can be grossed up?

alec.payroll: Relocation payments are typically taxable unless structured otherwise; we have a relocation policy with possible gross-up in specific cases (senior hires). I can't promise gross-up for an IC-level hire, but we can route through People Ops to see if relocation admin can be accommodated. Stipends/reimbursements issued after employment begins are processed through payroll and show on W-2.

carla-onboarding: If you upload docs now I can pre-stage your benefits enrollment so your 30-day window will start when you have an active hire date. If payroll needs to pause pay, carriers usually still allow enrollment to proceed in parallel, but coverage effective date depends on carrier rules and proof of work auth — I'll confirm with carriers and DM you.

jess.peopleops: Next steps: Maria upload to onboarding portal (scan of I-20 with travel signature, USCIS receipt notice, passport bio page). Alec will prepare the payroll acknowledgement template; Raj will advise on travel risk language; Carla will pre-stage benefits. We'll reconvene if anything changes. Thanks!

hr-bot: Reminder: please do NOT send original passports or I-9 docs via Slack. Use onboarding portal or secure upload.

maria.gonzalez: Uploaded docs and signed ACK on the portal. Thanks everyone. I'll keep you posted if travel changes.

jess.peopleops: Got it — we see the uploads. Safe travels if you go, and we'll flag payroll to hold pay until EAD provided per the ACK. :thumbsup:
